items.title: [Work In Progress] AMWA IN-004: Flow Orchestration and Monitoring Requirements
items.text: This repository holds the source of a work artifact published as an AMWA Increment (IN) from the Advanced Media Workflow Association
path: [Work In Progress] AMWA IN-004: Flow Orchestration and Monitoring Requirements

items.title: What does it do?
items.text:
• Defines the functional and non-functional requirements for a control API that manages MXL Readers and Writers in a DMF environment.
  • Builds on IN-001
  • Identifies gaps for further work
path: [Work In Progress] AMWA IN-004: Flow Orchestration and Monitoring Requirements

items.title: Why does it matter?
items.text: • MXL does not define a control API, so documenting requirements will help promote interoperability.
path: [Work In Progress] AMWA IN-004: Flow Orchestration and Monitoring Requirements

items.title: How does it work?
items.text:
• Gives requirements for setting paramters and querying status of MXL Writers and Readers.

This work artifact is published as an AMWA Increment (IN). Increments are intended to make public the ongoing progress of a working group without locking decisions into a formal specification. While the technical details contained in this repository do not constitute a stable or finalized specification, readers should note that Increments are Draft Specifications as defined in the AMWA IPR Policy. The provisions of the policy apply, including the requirement for early disclosure. You can expect the content to evolve incrementally based on ongoing testing, consensus-building, and community input. Public review is encouraged! Please post an Issue to the Repo to submit questions, feedback, or propose changes.

items.title: MXL Domains
items.text:
• An MXL domain is a folder in a tmpfs backed volume or filesystem that contains flows and grains (see MXL Architecture).
  • Multiple MXL domains can co-exist on the same host but each MXL domain exists only on one host (because it is a unique folder in the individual file system. The same path could exist on another host, but it would still be a different domain).
  • One or more MXL domains on a host can be mapped into the containers that host the media functions during deployment.
  • The path where the MXL domain is mapped need not be the same across different media function containers.
  • To be able to uniquely identify a domain, each domain contains a file “domain_def.json” (see AMWA BCP-007-03: NMOS With MXL) which needs to be created by the entity creating the MXL Domain (folder).

items.title: Usage
items.text:
• It is recommended to keep the MXL domain structure as simple as possible.
  • One MXL domain per host is a good starting point, if it meets the requirements.
  • Multiple MXL domains can be used for grouping flows for access control, e.g.
  • Flows internal to a PCR in one MXL domain, flows external in another MXL domain.
  • Different MXL domains for different productions.
  • Access control can be enforced by mapping only those MXL domains into a container that the media function needs access to or by means of UNIX file system permissions which give more granular control.

items.title: Domain Group
items.text:
• Since MXLDomains cannot span more than one host, an orchestration/control system may chose to establish a Domain Group that is a logical grouping of MXLDomain(s) (e.g. with similar access rights) possibly on different hosts. This does not imply replication of all the flows in the MXLDomain.
%% IN-004 "MXL Domains" and "Domain Group"

%% Host 2's pcr domain and flows A and B are the ones used in connect-sequence and monitoring-sequence.

items.title: MXL Flows
items.text:
• Media functions may need to create additional or new flows during runtime for a variety of reasons:
  • Reconfiguration
  • Change of input signal (for a gateway media function)

If that happens, the orchestration/control system should be notified of the new flows.

  • If the technical parameters of a flow change, the existing flow needs to be removed and a new flow (with a different flowID) needs to be created. If that is the case, the Media Function should notify the orchestration/control system that the writer is now writing a different flowID so that it can decide on the necessary actions:
  • inform the readers that were reading the original flow to now read the new flow
  • change the setup of the replication to now replicate the new flow instead of the original flow
  • When a writer shuts down, it needs to remove the flow folder and all its contents from the file system. Readers need to be able to cope with flows disappearing.
  • To prevent writers from deleting data that has not been read yet by readers downstream, they wait for at least one length of the ring buffer after having written the last data before shutting down and deleting the ring buffer.
  • The MXL SDK provides a function to clean the filesystem of any flow directories left over from writers that have not exited gracefully. This function needs to be called either periodically (e.g. a cron job) or when the need arises (e.g. through a watchdog) depending on the requirements of the concrete system.

items.title: Connecting and Disconnecting Flows
items.text:
• NMOS IS-05 (AMWA BCP-007-03: NMOS With MXL ) or other protocols following the flow connection API requirements specification can be used to connect and disconnect flows at runtime.
  • To be able to create DMFs with only static connections that do not require a separate realtime control system, media functions should provide a method to load a configuration file with the following yaml syntax when the container is deployed. 
senders:  
  1b99dffd-5412-4c69-9758-f7aee1143ad5:  
    master_enable: true  
    transport_params:  
      - mxl_domain_id: 0cb2af47-0e9e-47dc-8633-c451b353d02f  
        mxl_flow_id: 83df0a80-92d1-489d-a82b-077e2cef74cd

  ecaf4b73-c8bf-434a-902e-a55faf7f79e6:  
    master_enable: true  
    transport_params:  
      - mxl_domain_id: auto  
        mxl_flow_id: auto

receivers:  
  9c46ca50-f0ef-420a-949c-d490f76a9e9f:  
    master_enable: true  
    sender_id: bd156ddf-662e-40a7-9caa-b4bfe26c78a3  
    transport_params:  
      - mxl_domain_id: d9becfc9-c435-4bf7-abcc-59eed9a17028

items.title: Behaviour on Stopping and Restarting MXLWriters and MXLReaders
items.text:
This adds to behaviour described in IN-001:

  • When instructed to stop, an MXLWriter must stop writing data immediately and must stop advancing the head index. The flow folder must not be deleted.
  • When instructed to stop, an MXLReader must stop reading data immediately.
  • When instructed to (re-)start, an MXLReader must start reading according to the guidance in the the MXL documentation.
  • When instructed to (re-)start, an MXLWriter must start writing according to the guidance in the the MXL documentation.
flowchart TB
    subgraph Writer["MXLWriter"]
        direction LR
        WRun["Running<br/>Writing data and advancing head"]
        WStop["Stopped<br/>No writing<br/>Head index not advancing<br/>Flow folder retained"]
        WEnd["Shut down<br/>Flow folder removed"]

        WRun -->|Stop| WStop
        WStop -->|Restart| WRun
        WRun -->|Shut down after buffer drain| WEnd
        WStop -->|Shut down| WEnd
    end

    subgraph Reader["MXLReader"]
        direction TB
        RRun["Running<br/>Reading grains / samples"]
        RStop["Stopped<br/>No reading"]

        RRun -->|Stop| RStop
        RStop -->|Restart| RRun
    end

items.title: Replication
items.text:
Replication designates the process of copying the flow data from one domain to another.

  • The MXL SDK provides functions for this, however each domain needs a process that executes the necessary functions in the SDK.
  • Replication can be setup manually or automatically.
  • Replication can be setup statically (at deployment-time) or dynamically (on request during runtime)
  • Whoever sets up the replication is responsible for tearing it down when it is no longer needed (e.g. reader stops reading, writer exits, writer crashes etc.)

items.title: Between-Host Bandwidth Management
items.text:
• While inside one host or node bandwidth is considered unlimited, when replicating flows between hosts, the entity configuring the replication needs to take into account the limited bandwidth that is available for the replication.
  • For sake of simplicity, we assume at this point that the replication is managed centrally for each node and not by each media function individually.
  • Flow Bandwidth: The entity controlling the replication needs to be aware of the bandwidth required by each flow that needs to be replicated. Information about calculating the bandwidth is available in the MXL SDK.
  • Network Bandwidth: It still needs to be determined how the entity controlling the replication get information about the available bandwidth.
  • If there is not enough bandwidth available for a replication request the user who initiated the request needs to be notified. The means are still to be discussed.

items.title: Media Functions
items.text:
• Media Functions must be able to run in non-privileged containers.
  • Media Functions should be run in non-privileged containers.

items.title: Monitoring
items.text:
(Concentrating particularly on writers and readers rather than network issues etc.)

Provide monitoring of:

  • Media function writers
  • Media function readers
  • Replication (to be defined).

Notification of errors including:

  • For readers:
  • Access Status
    • Cannot access the required domain
    • Cannot access the required flow
  • Read Status
    • Grain/samples not available yet (as per MXL_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE_TOO_EARLY)
    • Grain/samples read too late (as per MXL_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE_TOO_LATE)
    • Grain/samples available but cannot be read:
    • Permission error
    • Other

  • Essence Status

    • Grain/samples available but wrong (e.g. wrong format, resolution, rate, illegal values etc.)

  • For writers:

  • Access Status
    • Cannot access the required domain
    • Cannot access the required flow
  • Write Status
    • Input Grain/samples available and correct but cannot be written to buffer
    • Permission error
    • Out of space
    • Other
  • Essence Status
    • Nothing available in time to write
    • Incorrect input (e.g. wrong format, resolution, rate, illegal values etc.)

Protocols a media function could use to provide those notifications could be:

  • NMOS IS-12
  • OpenTelemetry
  • ST 2138

Counters for the errors above, and also correct operation (e.g. correctly sent/received Grains).

If monitoring is supported, all the above statuses are mandatory. Counters are optional.

It is optional to support additional, more in-depth monitoring, for example via telemetry.

Media functions provide measurement of latency and jitter. The current MXL SDK does not provide this information directly but grain timestamps and the mxl-info tool in MXL SDK will help. TBD: we need a documented and common method of calculating this.

items.title: Examples
items.text: The following sequence diagrams show examples of Flow Connection and Monitoring.

items.title: Flow Connection
items.text:
%% IN-004 "Connecting and Disconnecting Flows" and "MXL Flows"
%% SDK calls from MXL lib/include/mxl/mxl.h and flow.h.
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant oc as Orchestration /<br/>control system
    participant wr as Writer media<br/>function
    participant rd as Reader media<br/>function
    participant pcr as MXL domain: pcr
    participant fa as Flow A
    participant fb as Flow B

    rect rgb(247, 246, 242)
        Note over oc,fb: container deployed: configuration file with static connections
        oc->>rd: map MXL domain into the container
        oc->>rd: configuration file (yaml): receivers, master_enable,<br/>transport_params: mxl_domain_id, mxl_flow_id = flow A
        rd->>pcr: mxlCreateInstance(domain path)
        rd->>fa: mxlCreateFlowReader(instance, flow A)
        loop per grain
            rd->>fa: mxlFlowReaderGetGrain(reader, index, timeout)
            fa-->>rd: grain
        end
    end

    rect rgb(238, 237, 254)
        Note over oc,fb: technical parameters of a flow change
        wr->>fb: create new flow (different flowID)
        wr->>oc: notify: writer is now writing a different flowID
        oc->>rd: IS-05 (BCP-007-03): read the new flow<br/>mxl_domain_id, mxl_flow_id = flow B
        rd->>fa: mxlReleaseFlowReader(instance, reader)
        rd->>fb: mxlCreateFlowReader(instance, flow B)
        wr->>fa: remove the original flow
        Note over rd,fa: readers need to be able to cope with flows disappearing
    end

    rect rgb(238, 237, 254)
        Note over oc,fb: disconnect at runtime
        oc->>rd: IS-05 (BCP-007-03): master_enable = false
        rd->>fb: mxlReleaseFlowReader(instance, reader)
    end

items.title: Monitoring
items.text:
%% IN-004 "Monitoring", reader side (same reader, domain and flow as connect-sequence)
%% SDK calls and status codes from MXL lib/include/mxl/mxl.h.
sequenceDiagram
    participant oc as Orchestration /<br/>control system
    participant rd as Reader media<br/>function
    participant pcr as MXL domain: pcr
    participant fa as Flow A

    rect rgb(250, 236, 231)
        Note over rd,fa: Access status
        rd->>pcr: mxlCreateInstance(domain path)
        pcr--xrd: cannot access the required domain
        rd->>fa: mxlCreateFlowReader(instance, flow A)
        fa--xrd: cannot access the required flow
    end

    loop per grain
        rd->>fa: mxlFlowReaderGetGrain(reader, index, timeout)
        alt correct operation
            fa-->>rd: grain
        else Read status
            fa--xrd: grain/samples not available yet<br/>(MXL_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE_TOO_EARLY)
        else Read status
            fa--xrd: grain/samples read too late<br/>(MXL_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE_TOO_LATE)
        else Read status
            fa--xrd: grain/samples available but cannot be read<br/>(permission error, other)
        end
        rd->>rd: Essence status: grain/samples available but wrong<br/>(e.g. wrong format, resolution, rate, illegal values)
    end

    rd->>oc: notification of errors, counters, latency and jitter (calculation TBD)<br/>NMOS IS-12, OpenTelemetry or ST 2138

    Note over oc,fa: provide monitoring of: media function writers, media function readers, replication
